How does an AI draw a picture out of pure static?
Tools like Stable Diffusion and Midjourney start with nothing but random noise.
Here's the trick: training runs backwards. Take a real photo, and add a little noise.
Add more, step after step, until the photo is buried in static.
At every step, the AI sees the noisy image and answers one question: what noise was just added?
It guesses, gets scored, and slowly learns what noise looks like, and what hides underneath.
Now to draw, start from pure static, and subtract the noise it predicts, a little at a time.
A sunrise appears from nothing. Your words steer every step, so the static becomes what you asked for.
So the AI never copies a picture. It learns the way back from chaos.
